title: Long subject lines break MailTransport
body:
This issue is a continuation of https://cakephp.lighthouseapp.com/projects/42648/tickets/2824-long-subject-lines-break-mailtransport.
// Currently this link died?

I built CentOS and qmail server and reproduced this issue.
CentOS 5.9
Apache 2.2.3
PHP 5.4.20
CakePHP 2.4.1
Qmail 1.03.5

case 1:
CakeEmail -> MailTransport -> mail() of PHP -> qmail-inject -> qmail-remote -(SMTP *1)-> Other SMTP Server
Outgoing SMTP packets have CRCRLF (at *1).

case 2:
CakeEmail -> MailTransport -> mail() of PHP -> qmail-inject -> qmail-local -> Maildir( *2) -> qmail-pop3d -(POP3)-> MUA( *3)
Message in mailbox has CRLF (at *2) . And some headers overflow to mail body in MUA (at *3).

sendmail command which is wrapper of qmail requires LF text. (*4)
http://www.lifewithqmail.org/lwq.html#cr
PHP must output LF text to 'sendmail_path'.

To output text with LF, 'to', 'subject', 'message' and 'headers' arguments of mail() must have LF.
If 'to' and 'subject' have LF, LF is converted to a SPACE(0x20) in mail() function.(*5)

``` C
cf. ext/standard/mail.c
        SKIP_LONG_HEADER_SEP(to_r, i);
        SKIP_LONG_HEADER_SEP(subject_r, i);
```

// If they have CRLF, CRLF is passed to 'sendmail_path' without change. And headers overflow to mail body.

Current implementation:
Use LF for EOL. Use CRLF to divide each subject and email header line.
Fault: message has CRLF.

Workaround:
Use SmtpTransport.
SMTP requires CRLF(RFC 5321).
SmrpTransport uses CRLF for EOL. And mb_encode_mimeheader divides by CRLF.

Solution 1 for MailTransport:
Use LF for EOL.
And use zero-length-string to divide each subject and email header line.
Fault: There is a possibility of exceed 998 bytes(RFC 5322).

Solution 2 for MailTransport:
Use LF at all line break.
Fault: LF in 'to' and 'subject' is replaced by SPACE(0x20).

(*4)
qmail requires LF.
Postfix seems to judge CRLF or LF using end of line of line 1.
Some POP3 servers replace like this: s/(CR)?LF/CRLF/  It negates this issue.

(*5) This is a strange behavior.
CRLF[ |\t]+ is passed through. LF[ |\t]+ is not passed through. But mail() outputs "\n" as header line break.

``` C
cf. ext/standard/mail.c
        fprintf(sendmail, "To: %s\n", to);
        fprintf(sendmail, "Subject: %s\n", subject);
```

This has been reported by user. But it is not modified until now. https://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=47983

A patch for use LF at all line break.

``` PHP
diff -ru cakephp-2.4.1.orig/lib/Cake/Network/Email/MailTransport.php cakephp-2.4.1.test/lib/Cake/Network/Email/MailTransport.php
--- cakephp-2.4.1.orig/lib/Cake/Network/Email/MailTransport.php 2013-09-15 11:07:19.000000000 +0900
+++ cakephp-2.4.1.test/lib/Cake/Network/Email/MailTransport.php 2013-10-16 21:53:14.000000000 +0900
@@ -39,12 +39,19 @@
        }
        $headers = $email->getHeaders(array('from', 'sender', 'replyTo', 'readReceipt', 'returnPath', 'to', 'cc', 'bcc'));
        $to = $headers['To'];
+       $to = str_replace("\r\n", $eol, $to); // replace CRLF from mb_encode_mimeheader
        unset($headers['To']);
+
+       foreach ($headers as $key => $value) {
+           $headers[$key] = str_replace("\r\n", $eol, $value); // replace CRLF from mb_encode_mimeheader
+       }
        $headers = $this->_headersToString($headers, $eol);
+       $subject = $email->subject();
+       $subject = str_replace("\r\n", $eol, $subject); // replace CRLF from mb_encode_mimeheader
        $message = implode($eol, $email->message());

        $params = isset($this->_config['additionalParameters']) ? $this->_config['additionalParameters'] : null;
-       $this->_mail($to, $email->subject(), $message, $headers, $params);
+       $this->_mail($to, $subject, $message, $headers, $params);
        return array('headers' => $headers, 'message' => $message);
    }


```
